searchText: I just would like to confirm something, does the `diff` in https://notes.ethereum.org/8LbisMwtR4yK64SBosb_2g#D1---Distance-Function function body means `node_id - content_id` ? I get the impression that diff is supposed to be delta (or the other way around). I'm not 100% though Hello, I will join the call today but I will be on mute, I have a sore throat and don’t feel well. On my side, I was working on PRs for extracting a core package for trin and bootstrapping the chain history crate. PR is also pushed for fixing a small bug which prevented trin to ping the bootstrap node. Next, I will work on implementing ACCEPT, OFFER and STORE messages for trin-history and then probably join <@!755612893046636585> on exploring the testing framework. Gonna be a few minutes late. Still dropping off kids at camp. Can we push this mornings sync meeting back 10 minutes? Alternatively, you guys can start without me I'm good to start late wont be joining today. was tied up to other stuffs in the past week https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82763999854?pwd=Uy9sR1ZxeUJhc0crckFKanV5VERCdz09 implementers call link for today The simplest idea for a starting point from my perspective seems to be having each client be able to run a bootnode that support PING/PONG/FIND/FOUND to allow establishing the DHT. This allows us to establish a public test network of long lived nodes sorry i couldn't make it today. i've been working on implementing advertise & requestProofs for Trin client, and also I've begun exploring the creation of a testing framework and will probably join forces with ognyan in the near future how would we accomplish this so that the nodes be long lived? i am working on writing a script that starts a trin client, greps the logs for the enr of the node, and then takes that enr to use it as a bootnode enr when starting a second client. then that pair of nodes can pass network msgs between each other, but i'm confused on how to make the bootnodes long lived? It should be possible to write the client in such a way that the bootnodes somewhat ignore the *extra* protocol messages, so the bootnodes in theory can be long lived and semi stable. The other nodes in the network can come-and-go, but it would allow us to test in a public testnetwork <@!694014391288332358> just realized that OFFER/ACCEPT/STORE doesn't fit cleanly into the discv5 request/response paradigm. I think this is ok, but probably worth pointing out because this would be yet another place where we would be going against the *base* protocol's un-enforceable rule that all requests have a corresponding response messages. I think the right way forward is to submit a patch to the base protocol definition to loosen this from a MUST to a SHOULD with some context. That’s a good callout. Off the top of my head I guess the alternative is to use some form of ack message (eg STORED)? The ACK simply to comply with the request/response seems un-necessary so I'd say the default course of action would be to simply have STORE exist without a response message and to acknowledge the diversion from the stated rules of the base protocol in the spec. The uTP messages are likely to do the same thing (all TALKREQ, no TALKRESP) so unless we're going to comply across the board, I don't think we need to start inserting response message types where they aren't strictly needed. That makes sense. Just wanted to make sure it was considered and better understand the reasoning. I’ll make sure I acknowledge this in the history spec this before raising the PR Ok, I've completed a simple first pass on my document: https://notes.ethereum.org/8LbisMwtR4yK64SBosb_2g?view I attempt to outline all the functionality needed by a client on a decently granular level. I'd be curious to get some 👀 from any of the implementation teams on 1) whether you think this resource will be useful to you and 2) whether there's anything outlined there that you have questions about and 3) whether there is anything that you see that I missed. this is state network specific but <@!694014391288332358> if you want to look over my sections that cover the OFFER/ACCEPT/STORE it is relatively simple to map those onto the chain history network instead. re: <@783601578779082753> question earlier in this channel - <@!364458974906548225> in the `return` statements for the new distance function, is `diff == delta`? <@!439193900096290816> <@!783601578779082753> yes, that was a typo. I've updated the document to reflect that. Also added the stackoverflow answer that I pulled the structure/logic of that function from and a few example test cases.

excerpts.content: how would we accomplish this so that the nodes be long lived? i am working on writing a script that starts a trin client, greps the logs for the enr of the node, and then takes that enr to use it as a bootnode enr when starting a second client. then that pair of nodes can pass network msgs between each other, but i'm confused on how to make the bootnodes long lived?

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: It should be possible to write the client in such a way that the bootnodes somewhat ignore the *extra* protocol messages, so the bootnodes in theory can be long lived and semi stable.  The other nodes in the network can come-and-go, but it would allow us to test in a public testnetwork
